name: read-path-contract
body:
Source: `lbug-lock-race/feedback-13` (phase-level) — `read-access-during-session` was under-specified for a non-routing reader and offered an unrealizable "open the DB without contending" alternative; `read-your-writes` carried "no shared session state" wording that conflicts with read-through routing.

Chosen contract [with user] — feedback option (a), routing is the read mechanism while a session is live:
1. While a session owns `db.lbug`, the coordinator owns the DB and reads are served by routing to the live session (`apg query` / suite tools detect it and forward). This is what `global.constraint.immediate-queryability` guarantees for a routed reader.
2. A non-routing reader that opens `db.lbug` directly during a live session is OUT of contract: lbug's contended open ERRORS ("Could not set lock"), it does not wait. It must route via the tool or be retried after the session ends. The spec no longer implies a non-contending direct open.
3. When no session is live, the DB file is not held and any reader opens it normally and sees committed mutations — the direct path that `read-your-writes` covers. The "no shared session state" phrasing is reconciled: read-through routing is transparent and is not prior coordination the caller supplies.
4. `coordinator-single-writer`'s read-only-opener wording is scoped to ROUTED readers (routed reads keep working); it no longer claims a direct contended open "waits".

Nodes revised: `requirements.requirement.read-access-during-session`, `requirements.requirement.read-your-writes`, `requirements.requirement.coordinator-single-writer`, `solution.component.session-routing`, `domain.service.graph-read`, and `global.constraint.one-commit-per-mutation` (residual "batching the derived-projection flush is free" removed — the law is now purely about commit batching and defers projection visibility to `immediate-queryability`). The plan-writer aligns `plan.phase-03.task-22` and adds the non-routing case to task-23. [with user]
